## Answer

**Launch-time behavior (Node.js 22.0.0, 2024‑04‑24).** The v22 launch announcement described this as a new capability: "This release adds `require()` support for synchronous ESM graphs under the flag `--experimental-require-module`." It applied only if the module was "Explicitly marked as an ES module with a `"type": "module"` field in the closest package.json or a `.mjs` extension" and was "Fully synchronous (contains no top-level await)." The announcement explicitly said the project intended "to eventually enable `require(esm)` by default in the future, without the flag" (nodejs.org v22 release announcement; nodejs.org/en/blog/release/v22.0.0).

**22.12.0 (LTS, 2024‑12‑03).** The release notes for exactly v22.12.0 lead with the notable change "require(esm) is now enabled by default": support "had been available on v20.x and v22.x under the command line flag `--experimental-require-module`… In this release, it is now no longer behind a flag on v22.x." The corresponding commit is `58d6871c45` — "(SEMVER-MINOR) module: unflag --experimental-require-module" (#55085), and "Contributed by Joyee Cheung in #55085."

**Does default-on make it stable? No.** The same v22.12.0 notes state plainly: "This feature is still experimental, and we are looking for user feedback to make more final tweaks before fully stabilizing it." So enabling by default is not the same as marking it stable; it remained experimental in 22.12.0. (The docs for that version show the ESM page as "Stability: 2 - Stable" overall, but the specific `require` section only says the CommonJS `require` "currently only supports loading synchronous ES modules (that is, ES modules that do not use top-level `await`)" — no stability-2 designation is asserted for require(esm) itself.) Note a wording wrinkle: the nodejs.org release-note prose says "on v23.x" for the experimental-warning sentence, whereas the GitHub changelog (nodejs/node CHANGELOG_V22, PR #56040) says "on v22.x" — the v22.x wording is the consistent one for this release.

**Top-level await error.** With the feature enabled, Node.js "will no longer throw `ERR_REQUIRE_ESM` if `require()` is used to load a ES module. It can, however, throw `ERR_REQUIRE_ASYNC_MODULE` if the ES module being loaded or its dependencies contain top-level `await`." (This matches the launch-time condition that the graph must be fully synchronous.) When loading succeeds, the returned object "will either be a ES module namespace object similar to what's returned by `import()`, or what gets exported as `"module.exports"` in the ES module."

**Disabling flag.** "this feature can also be disabled using `--no-experimental-require-module` as a workaround" (v22.12.0 notes).

**Runtime feature check documented for 22.12.0.** "Users can check `process.features.require_module` to see whether `require(esm)` is enabled in the current Node.js instance." For packages, the `"module-sync"` exports condition can detect `require(esm)` support so both `require()` and `import` can load the same native ES module.

**Reconciliation summary.** Launch (22.0.0): opt-in behind `--experimental-require-module`, synchronous-only. 22.12.0: flag removed on v22.x, enabled by default — but still experimental, just as the launch announcement anticipated ("eventually enable… by default"). The feature is not stabilized by default-on in this release.

**Limitations.** I verified the v22 launch announcement and the exact 22.12.0 release notes plus the versioned ESM docs; the precise stability label wording for the dedicated "Loading ECMAScript modules using require()" doc page was not fully retrieved (the ESM page fetch truncated before that subsection), and the release-notes prose contains the v22.x/v23.x inconsistency noted above. No later Node release's behavior was used.
